title: Golden Ratio and the Fibonacci Sequence
subject: Mathematics
objective: Count a sunflower's seed spirals and you often get 34 and 55. They come from the Fibonacci sequence, whose ratios settle on the golden ratio, 1.618…

fill.q: In the Fibonacci sequence, each term is the ____ of the two terms before it.
The golden ratio is written with the Greek letter ____.
Sunflower seeds grow about ____ degrees apart.

tf.q: 13/8 is closer to the golden ratio than 3/2.
Every flower has a Fibonacci number of petals.
Seeds placed 135° apart pack without gaps.
tf.explain: 135° is 3/8 of a turn, so seeds line up in 8 spokes with gaps.

ar.a: Sunflower seeds fill the head without gaps.
ar.r: Each seed grows about 137.5° from the last.
Each term is the sum of the two before it.
ar.explain: R explains A: that rule makes the ratio settle on φ.

short.q: Explain how the golden spiral is drawn.
short.solution: Tile squares of sides 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 into a rectangle, then draw a quarter circle in each square, joined end to end.
